title: Counter-Selector Wave 31: recipient-acknowledged handoff controls
purpose: Strengthen the public handoff calibration set with two named incoming operators who explicitly acknowledged handover events and one matched authority-before-access control. Separate acknowledgment of a meeting, role, or state category from acknowledgment of a complete recoverable package.

complete_direct_handoff_requires: attributable recipient acknowledgment of the package rather than only the role or meeting
authority, credentials, dependencies, and open decisions inventoried
rollback, refusal, and safe-decline conditions preserved
successor action observed from the transferred state
continuity observed without hidden focal-person state

controls.public_label: recipient-acknowledged elected project-leader handover with partial state categories
controls.authorizing_body: Debian Developers election under the Debian Constitution

source_records.title: Debian Project Leader Elections 2020
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves the election process, candidates, ballots, and result surface for the incoming leader.

source_records.title: DPL elections 2020, congratulations Jonathan Carter!
source_records.artifact_scope: Names the elected successor, term start, and outgoing leader.

source_records.title: Bits from the new DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: The incoming leader states that he and the outgoing leader held a handover meeting and names finances, delegations, legal matters, outreach, and other questions as discussed state categories.

source_records.title: DPL Activity logs for April/May 2020
source_records.artifact_scope: The incoming leader records the handover session and a first-month sequence of decisions, delegation work, financial coordination, and external representation.

source_records.title: Debian Project Leader
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines the DPL role, election mechanism, coordination responsibilities, delegation authority, urgent decisions, and financial duties.

source_records.title: Debian Constitution
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines the Project Leader's powers, appointment, resignation, delegation, and decision authority.

counterevidence: The public record describes a meeting and subject categories, not an itemized outgoing state package.
No public inventory of credentials, access, dependencies, open decisions, or pending deadlines was located.
No rollback, refusal, safe-decline, or emergency-access conditions were located.
The successor activity log proves operation after the transition but not that each action arose from transferred state.
The principal handover evidence is the incoming participant's own public account rather than an independent audit.
falsifiers: evidence that no handover meeting occurred
evidence that the named incoming person did not assume the role
evidence that the listed responsibility categories were not discussed
a public itemized outgoing package and recipient acknowledgment that would justify a stronger handoff state

controls.public_label: recipient-acknowledged elected project-leader handover with stated open items
controls.authorizing_body: Debian Developers election under the Debian Constitution

source_records.title: Debian Project Leader Elections 2026: Call for nominations
source_records.artifact_scope: Defines the constitutional election timeline and the date on which the new leader's term begins.

source_records.title: Debian Project Leader Election 2026 Results
source_records.artifact_scope: Names the incoming leader selected by the developer vote.

source_records.title: Bits from the DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: The outgoing leader states that he will not run again and expects to hand duties to the incoming candidate if elected.

source_records.title: (A short) Bits from the new DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: The incoming leader says she took charge, describes a smooth video-call handover, and names re-delegations, a time-limited delegation, DPL Helpers, and platform topics as open work.

source_records.title: Bits from past DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: The former leader publicly addresses the incoming leader after the term transition and treats the prior term as ended.

source_records.title: Debian Project Leader
source_records.artifact_scope: Lists the incoming person as the current Debian Project Leader and preserves the role's authority and task surface.

counterevidence: A statement that the handover was smooth does not identify the package, credentials, dependencies, or deadlines transferred.
The listed delegations, helpers, and platform topics are a partial open-work surface, not a complete decision inventory.
No public rollback, refusal, emergency-access, or safe-decline conditions were located.
Current role occupancy does not prove independent resumability from a transferred state package.
The incoming and outgoing messages are participant-authored rather than an independent handoff audit.
falsifiers: evidence that the video handover did not occur
evidence that the incoming person did not assume the role
evidence that the listed open items were not inherited work
a public complete package, recipient acknowledgment, and successor action chain that would justify a stronger handoff state

controls.public_label: formal delegated authority preceding operational access and later team operation
controls.outgoing_entity: FTP Master delegation and Archive Operations holders
controls.authorizing_body: Debian Project Leader delegation under Debian Constitution section 8

source_records.title: New delegation for DFSG, Licensing & New Packages Team
source_records.artifact_scope: Creates the new delegated team, names members, revokes the previous FTP Master delegation, and defines continuing authority.

source_records.title: Bits from the DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: States that candidate team members were training on NEW packages without direct access to the NEW queue.

source_records.title: Bits from the DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: States that the handover was in progress, technical details remained under discussion, and the future team lacked queue access before formal delegation.

source_records.title: New delegation for DFSG, Licensing & New Packages Team (superseding previous announcement)
source_records.artifact_scope: Supersedes the earlier announcement and establishes the active delegated team and responsibility surface.

source_records.title: Bits from the DPL
source_records.artifact_scope: States that access and operational details were not immediately available after delegation and that technical and procedural handover steps completed only later.

source_records.title: Bits from the DFSG Team: New Dashboard & Queue Processes
source_records.artifact_scope: The incoming team states that it is operational, describes the dashboard and queue process, and credits Archive Operations and DSA support.

counterevidence: Formal delegation occurred before complete access and operational details were available.
Training without direct queue access did not constitute operational custody.
Later operation depended on Archive Operations, DSA, infrastructure, and tooling support.
No complete outgoing state package, recipient acknowledgment, dependency inventory, or rollback package was located.
Eventual operation does not erase the timing gap between authority and usable state.
falsifiers: evidence that the incoming team had complete operational access at delegation
evidence that no access or procedural delay occurred
evidence that the team never became operational
a public complete package and acknowledgment showing timely authority-and-state transfer

next_action: Apply the recipient-acknowledgment ladder to candidate lanes and acquire public outgoing packages, itemized dependencies and open decisions, credential transfer, rollback conditions, and recipient acknowledgment of the package without contacting source subjects.
